audit.whatIsWrong: Chart gave Irelia six of seven stages while its own whys say 'you both start soft' at 1, 'the lane evens out' at 4-5, 'you own this level' at 6, 'she needs a lead you deny by playing even' at first item and 'even game' at two items. The full layer also read HARD 7.5/10 against a 51.65% win rate over 393 games.
audit.why: Irelia genuinely owns 2-3 on Bladesurge resets off the wave and Flawless Duet, but Vorpal Spikes clear and Carnivore stabilise 4-5, and Feast is a true-damage answer to her dive at 6. Beyond that it is a coinflip that hinges on whether she got a lead.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill / Irelia / Irelia / Skill / Cho'Gath / Skill / Skill; diff re-rated EVEN 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phase whys were generic template text with no cooldowns, and the level-6 line said only 'Irelia's ultimate changes the math too'.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, Bladesurge 10/9/8/7/6s but refreshed on a Marked target or a kill, Defiant Dance 20/18/16/14/12s, Vanguard's Edge 125/105/85s and Feast 80/70/60s. Vanguard's Edge at 125s rank 1 is the longest cooldown in the lane and was never mentioned once.
audit.corrected: Phase and cooldown fields now carry Flawless Duet 16s, Bladesurge 10s with its reset condition, Vanguard's Edge 125s and Feast 80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Interaction fields said only 'Her engage CC. Silence/dodge it.' The reset loop that actually decides the lane was never spelled out, and Vanguard's Edge's wall does not appear anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Riot's text: Flawless Duet Marks the targets it stuns, and Bladesurge's cooldown refreshes if the target is Marked or dies to it. So her E is not just a stun — it is what turns her Q into a free repeatable dash. Feral Scream (11/10.5/10/9.5/9s) silencing her mid-dash is what denies the reset, and Rupture's knockup takes her out of the dash itself. Vanguard's Edge leaves a damaging, slowing wall, and Cho'Gath has no dash to cross it — that is how she cuts off a retreat.
audit.corrected: Silence her mid-dash and Bladesurge cannot reset out; Vanguard's Edge walls off a retreat you cannot dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia is called 'he'/'his' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.trading, breakdown.wave, breakdown.feeding, report[3].t, report[4].t, report[12].t and report[8].t ('his healing fights your grind').
audit.why: Irelia is female, and the misgendering sits in the trading, wave and itemization advice.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in every field edited here; the anti-heal line now names Bladesurge as the heal it is answering.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Irelia contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: You both start soft — she opens Q, you open Q, neither has a sustain edge. Deny last-hits and set the wave; do not trade into her dash.

edits.before: W silence starts flipping his combo windows. Only take the trade when Irelia's Flawless Duet is down.
edits.after: Bladesurge resets off your wave, so she stacks Ionian Fervor and all-ins before Feral Scream exists.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Irelia must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Flawless Duet (16s at rank 1) stuns and Marks you, and a Marked target refreshes Bladesurge — concede this window.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Flawless Duet's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Rupture-into-Feral Scream, Vorpal Spikes clear and Carnivore all arrive — you heal off farm and the lane genuinely levels out.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Irelia's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast (80s) is point-blank true damage, so Defiant Dance's physical reduction barely blunts it. Bait Flawless Duet, then punish the dash-in with knockup and silence.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Flawless Duet's cooldown.
edits.after: Bami's plus Vorpal Spikes lets you shove and farm safely — she needs a lead you keep denying.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Irelia carry threat 9/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Even, your lockdown wins fights; fed, her Trinity Force and armour shred melt your stacks. Play grouped, not the duel.

edits.before: Track Irelia's Flawless Duet (Stun): Her engage CC. Silence/dodge it. When it is down — Q-W + R her.
edits.after: Silence her mid-dash and Bladesurge cannot reset out; Vanguard's Edge walls off a retreat you cannot dash.

notes: Irelia's kit file tags Flawless Duet (E) with 'grounding'; Riot's description says damaged, stunned and Marked, with no ground, so I did not assert it. Packet flagged whys[4] 'Defiant Dance's' as a probable wrong name — false positive. The reset condition (Bladesurge refreshes on a Marked target, and Flawless Duet is what applies the Mark) was absent from the whole entry and is the mechanical core of the matchup. Cho'Gath's kit flags Rupture as 'grounding'; Riot's text says it pops enemies into the air, so I wrote knockup.
